claim_set.claim_text: Every AI clinical answer that informs a clinical decision MUST map to a recorded authority-to-inform — the agent, the clinical purpose, and the patient context that authorised the AI to inform this decision. Answers lacking a recorded authority-to-inform are refused at the action-admissibility gate.

Every AI-assisted processing of patient health data (GDPR / UK GDPR Article 9 special-category data) MUST carry a recorded Article 9 lawful basis scoped to the declared clinical purpose. Processing without a recorded health lawful basis is refused.

A clinical AI operating as a regulated medical device (EU MDR / UK MHRA) or an EU AI Act Annex III high-risk health system MUST NOT enter clinical use unless a current conformity declaration is recorded — device classification, EU AI Act high-risk conformity assessment, and named placing-on-market authority.

Every material AI clinical answer that informs a clinical decision MUST emit a signed, replay-derivable Evidence Pack binding the agent and model version, the authority-to-inform exercised, the GDPR Art. 9 basis, the pinned sources, and the Authority Finality outcome.

An AI clinical answer MUST remain advisory and MUST NOT drive a clinical action until a named clinician review is recorded. Unreviewed AI-driven clinical actions are refused and routed dual-channel to the responsible clinician.
